content: We also propose a system called ALOHA (Artificial Learning On Human Attributes) as a novel method of incorporating HLAs into dialogue agents. ALOHA maps characters to a latent space based on their HLAs, determines which are most similar in profile and identity, and recovers language styles of specific characters. We test the performance of ALOHA in character language style recovery against four baselines, demonstrating outperformance and system stability. We also run a human evaluation supporting our results. Our major contributions are: (1) We propose HLAs as personality aspects of fictional characters from the audience's perspective based on tropes; (2) We provide a large dialogue dataset traceable back to both its context and associated human-like attributes; (3) We propose a system called ALOHA that is able to recommend responses linked to specific characters. We demonstrate that ALOHA, combined with the proposed dataset, outperforms baselines. ALOHA also shows stable performance regardless of the character's identity, genre of the show, and context of the dialogue. We plan to release all of ALOHA's data and code.
